question: Examine the system of constraints $2x+y\geq14$, $4x+2y\leq24$, $x\geq0$ and $y\geq0$. Show algebraically that no point can satisfy all the constraints simultaneously. Hence state the nature of the solution set.
explanation:
Step 1: Simplifying the second constraint
The inequality $$4x+2y\leq24$$ can be divided by $2$ to obtain $$2x+y\leq12$$
Step 2: Comparing the principal constraints
The first constraint requires $$2x+y\geq14$$ whereas the simplified second constraint requires $$2x+y\leq12$$
Step 3: Establishing incompatibility
No real value of $2x+y$ can be simultaneously at least $14$ and at most $12$. Thus, the two constraints are mutually inconsistent.
Step 4: Considering non-negative restrictions
The conditions $x\geq0$ and $y\geq0$ cannot remove this contradiction between the two principal inequalities.
Step 5: Conclusion
Therefore, there is no ordered pair $(x,y)$ satisfying all the constraints simultaneously. Hence, the problem has no feasible solution and consequently no feasible region; every point fails to satisfy the complete system.

options.A: The system has a bounded feasible region because $2x+y$ lies between $12$ and $14$
options.B: The system has an unbounded feasible region
options.C: The system has no feasible solution because it requires $2x+y\geq14$ and $2x+y\leq12$ simultaneously
options.D: The feasible set consists only of points satisfying $2x+y=13$
